# Niansia

<p class="role-line">Computer science student and research-minded engineer.</p>

I am a final-year student at **Yuan Ze University** working across computer vision, vision-language models, AI security, quantitative research, and machine learning.

I am most interested in the point where a convincing model becomes a dependable system: how evidence is collected, how reasoning fails, how uncertainty is communicated, and how an experiment can be reproduced by someone else.

::: {.section-block #research}
::: {.section-rail}
<span>01</span>
<h2>Research questions</h2>
:::

::: {.section-content}
<p class="section-lead">Three questions currently organize my work.</p>

::: {.question-list}
::: {.question-item}
<span class="question-index">A</span>
<div>
<h3>Visual memory and multimodal reasoning</h3>
<p>What visual evidence should a vision-language system retain across a long interaction, and which tests can separate grounded reasoning from a fluent guess?</p>
<p class="keywords">Computer vision · VLMs · memory · evaluation</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.question-item}
<span class="question-index">B</span>
<div>
<h3>Trust, provenance, and adversarial evidence</h3>
<p>How can model-assisted research preserve an inspectable evidence chain and make weak, missing, or historically invalid support visible?</p>
<p class="keywords">AI security · provenance · auditability · research integrity</p>
</div>
:::

::: {.question-item}
<span class="question-index">C</span>
<div>
<h3>Uncertainty in quantitative decisions</h3>
<p>How should forecasting and simulation systems surface uncertainty, scenario sensitivity, and downside risk without creating false precision?</p>
<p class="keywords">Quantitative ML · forecasting · simulation · risk</p>
</div>
:::
:::

<p class="quiet-note">These are active directions, not claims of completed research. I publish code and notes when the evidence is ready to be inspected.</p>
:::
:::

<div class="work-meta"><span>Research tool</span><span>2026</span></div>

### NoveltyAudit

An evidence-first agent skill for adversarial scholarly novelty audits. It decomposes claims, searches for minimal prior sets, applies historical cutoffs, and records bridge-dependent prior-work arguments.

<p class="work-links"><a href="https://github.com/niansia/NoveltyAudit">Code</a><span>/</span><a href="https://github.com/niansia/NoveltyAudit#readme">Documentation</a></p>
